thread:
Priya: Hey team, quick newbie question — I'm about to open my first PR touching runtime routing + a tiny config tweak. Do we prefer splitting runtime logic and config into separate PRs or keep as one? Trying to avoid a monster PR on day 1.

Nina: Welcome Priya! If it's one atomic behavior change (routing change + its config flag) keep it in one PR. If you're changing a schema/proto or public config shape, do the schema change first, then callers in a follow-up.

Sam: For size, aim for small, reviewable diffs. Our rough target is <400 LOC of product code. Tests can add lines — note that in the PR body. If it's >600 LOC add a short justification.

Priya: Good to know. What about reviewers and labels?

Sam: Add two reviewers: one CODEOWNER for impacted paths + a peer. Labels: `area/runtime`, `needs-review`. If it's latency-sensitive add `needs-perf` and ping @Alex.

Priya: Pre-commit stuff — my local mypy is failing with new stubs. CI will block merges?

ci-bot: Repo hooks: black, isort, mypy, flake8. CI enforces these and will block merges on failures. CI link: https://ci.redwood.example/job/1769990000

Alex: Run `make dev-setup` to install hooks, then `pre-commit run --all-files`. For exact CI flags try `mypy -p redwood --config-file=pyproject.toml`. If something's flaky, ping me and we can mirror CI locally.

Priya: Commit message style and branch naming?

Alex: Branch: `feature/<TICKET>-short-desc` or `fix/<TICKET>-short-desc`. Commit: `area(scope): short summary` — e.g., `runtime(router): debounce duplicate lookups`. Squash merges are OK for small fixes.

Priya: Any required PR body sections? Rollback examples?

Sam: Use the PR template. Include: brief description, test plan, rollback steps (1-2 lines), and perf notes. Example rollback: "revert PR -> deploy -> run `tools/cachectl invalidate --prefix=route:`". If perf changes are possible, add a p50/p95 note and who to alert.

Priya: Awesome. I'll open the PR and paste the link here. Thanks for the quick onboarding help! :smile:
